approach: Add `check_root_cause_diagnosis(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and register it as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_code_survey`. It applies when the reading has a capability, no question, class `code` or `tests`, at least one behavior criterion, and the request's trimmed non-bullet lines hold a repair word (fix, fixes, fixing, bug, bugs, or the phrase 'still shows'). It then requires (a) a root-cause criterion that says 'root cause', says where the wrong output enters or why it is not excluded, and names a concrete location (a backticked span, a crates/ path, or a repo-path token whose last segment has a file extension), and (b) a Behavior criterion that names a test and satisfies Athena's own existing predicate `asks_for_failing_run_without_the_fix` (run/mod.rs:174), made `pub(crate)` and called from the gate. That is the same predicate that makes Athena plan the job (run/mod.rs:863) and run the 'fails without the fix' demonstration itself, so the gate and the revert run cannot disagree. A criterion equal to one of the request's own bullets never counts. Add `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` and a seventh `READING_RULES` line in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, composed beside `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`. Add unit tests, corpus cases, a steward test, a CHANGELOG Fixed entry and a short docs/architecture.md paragraph. The gate reads only the reading and request, never the repository. Prompt files, records, xtask and the decisions page are untouched. Introspection fix requests ('Fix the root cause of a repeated failure', hestia.rs:434) are in scope by design.

decisions.choice: Fix it at the reading gate with a new `check_*` step in `refusing_check`, not in the decisions page code.
decisions.reason: Both rejected jobs (20261103-201526-t4qv, 20261103-231808-3gkq) moved a filter because the accepted reading never required a diagnosis or a test that fails on the base. The gate is where that reading was accepted. `refusing_check` is the single entry point and refusal_corpus.rs enforces one refusing case per step.

rejected.why: That is one instance; out of scope and the candidates are dropped.
The mechanism default requires a refusal, not prose alone.

decisions.choice: Detect a bug-fix job from the request's prose only. Trim each line, drop lines where `is_bullet` is true, lowercase, replace `_` with `x`, and match with `has_phrase`. The triggers sit in one const: fix, fixes, fixing, bug, bugs, and the phrase 'still shows'. 'regression', 'fixed', 'wrong', 'broken', 'already', 'fails' and 'failing' are NOT triggers. Introspection fix requests ('Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: ...', built in hestia.rs:434 and shaped in refusal_corpus.rs:218) trigger the check through 'fix'. This is by design: the root-cause user default says such a job names its cause and proves it with a test, so a code or tests reading of an introspection job needs the two criteria. The doc comment and CHANGELOG say so, and the 8% estimate is weighed with that share.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 3 and 4. 'regression' appears in 'add regression tests for X', a tests-only job that fixes nothing, so it is dropped. 'fixed', 'wrong' and 'broken' are ordinary in feature prose ('a fixed token budget', 'refuse a config with a wrong value', 'report broken links'). The example request 'The page lists proposals that were already decided; fix it' is still caught by 'fix'. Trimming before `is_bullet` makes an indented bullet count as a bullet, so its 'fails when ...' never triggers. Whole-word matching leaves 'prefix', 'fixture' and `fix_x` alone. A continuation line of a wrapped bullet counts as prose; the doc comment notes this limit.

rejected.why: Refuses 'add regression tests for X' readings of class tests, which fix nothing (finding 3).

rejected.option: Keep fixed, wrong and broken as triggers
Exempt introspection requests from the check
rejected.why: They are the class this job exists to stop: both introspections that motivated it came from jobs of this shape. An exemption would leave the gate open where the failure was seen.

rejected.option: Match the whole request text including bullets
rejected.why: Feature bullets with 'fails when' would be refused.
Changes the closed class list and config; the reader could pick another class and bypass it.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must (1) contain 'root cause' or 'root-cause', (2) contain a locator stem (where, enter, originat, why, exclud, because), (3) name a concrete location: a backticked code span, `names_crates_path` (reading.rs:3454), or a `path_tokens` (reading.rs:3035) token whose last segment holds a '.', and (4) not equal any request bullet after `normalised` (reading.rs:3906) with the marker removed. The base-failing-test criterion must be kind Behavior, satisfy `asks_for_failing_run_without_the_fix(&c.text)` (the existing predicate, moved to `pub(crate)` in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:174 and called from reading.rs as `crate::run::asks_for_failing_run_without_the_fix`), name a test (a backticked span, a crates/ path or 'cargo test'), and not equal a request bullet. No second phrase list is kept.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1 and 2 of the earlier rounds and finding 1 of this one. The predicate (fail* word plus ' without the fix/change/mechanism/patch/it ', ' before the fix ', ' on the base ', or 'fail* without') already decides which Behavior criteria make Athena plan the job (run/mod.rs:863) and run the revert demonstration (verification.rs:128). One predicate means a criterion the gate accepts is one Athena checks mechanically on a scratch copy, which is the mechanical half of 'the test fails on the base'. That is what job 20261103-231808-3gkq lacked. 'On the base tree' matches ' on the base '. `path_tokens` finds plain-text repo paths such as xtask/src/site.rs, which the motivating diagnoses needed. Requiring a '.' in the last segment keeps 'and/or' from counting. The stock bullets (refusal_corpus.rs:227-228) have no location and equal a request bullet, so copying them fails twice. Whether the test uses real approved and rejected data cannot be decided from text; the guide asks for it and the doc comment marks it prose-only.

rejected.option: A second phrase list in reading.rs ('base tree', 'base commit', 'before the change')
rejected.why: It disagrees with the revert-run predicate: 'fails before the change' would pass the gate with no revert run, and 'fails without it' would run but be refused (finding 1).

rejected.option: Accept only crates/ paths or backticked spans for the location
rejected.why: Refuses the xtask diagnoses that motivated the job.

rejected.option: Accept any criterion with 'root cause' plus a locator word

rejected.why: A template refuses good free-text readings.

rejected.option: Mechanically require real recorded data in the test criterion
rejected.why: Not decidable from text without false refusals.

decisions.choice: Put guidance in a new `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` constant plus a seventh `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs, and raise the section-size bound in the brief test. The guide tells the reader to write, in its own words and not the request's bullets, a root-cause criterion naming the file, function or data source where the wrong items enter and why they are not excluded, and a behavior criterion naming a test built from real recorded data of both kinds (approved and rejected) that 'fails on the base tree and passes with the change'.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks for a constant composed beside `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`. Every reading check has a rule line (briefs.rs test near 3965). The reader prompt set (1997 of 2000) and verifier set (1298 of 1300) have no headroom, and the briefs sit outside those sets (docs/system-facts.md).

rejected.why: No token headroom; out of scope.
The criterion asks for a separate constant.

decisions.choice: Declare the share in three places. Criterion 4 of the reading quotes 'expected 8% of newly refused readings'; `replay_declaration_of` (reading.rs:3979) reads the reading's `acceptance_criteria` and `out_of_scope`, and that is what the replay hold reads. The doc comment and CHANGELOG repeat the phrase for strangers, each followed by a separate sentence: 'This share is an estimate; the snapshot has no records, so no replay was run when it was written.' They also say introspection fix requests are in scope by design and add to the share.
decisions.reason: The doc comment and CHANGELOG do not feed the hold; they record intent. A unit test applies `replay_declaration_of` to a reading whose criterion 4 holds the sentence and asserts `share == Some(8)`, where '%' is followed by ' of newly refused' as `declared_percent` (reading.rs:3917) requires.

rejected.why: The replay would hold the job at 10% with no recorded intent.

decisions.choice: Add a unit test that builds this job's own reading shape (request prose with 'Fix the root cause', class code, brief criteria 1 and 4 as written) and asserts `check_reading_acceptance` accepts it.
decisions.reason: A retry or re-read of this job runs through the new gate. Criterion 4 says 'root cause', 'where', and names `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`. Criterion 1 is Behavior, names `cargo test`, says 'fails on the base tree' (matches ' on the base ' in the shared predicate), and equals no request bullet.

rejected.option: No check of the job's own reading
rejected.why: A gate that refuses its own job's reading would stall a retry.

decisions.choice: Hold queued proposed jobs whose stored reading now fails the new check, with no code change in steward.rs. `queued_work` (steward.rs:401-406) already leaves out a stored reading that fails `check_reading_text` until a person runs `athena go`. Cover it with a new steward test and name the effect in the CHANGELOG entry.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. The behavior is the documented one (steward.rs:380) and is intended: such a job is re-read under the new rule instead of being dispatched with a reading that has no diagnosis. The person who runs Athena must be told, so the CHANGELOG says so.

rejected.option: Exempt stored readings from the new check in queued_work
rejected.why: That would let old symptom-only readings through the drain, which is the failure class.

rejected.option: Change queued_work to re-read such jobs automatically
rejected.why: Out of scope; drain behavior is not changed by this job.

risks.risk: A feature request uses 'fix' or 'bug' as an ordinary word in its prose and is refused.
risks.mitigation: The triggers are narrow (fix, fixes, fixing, bug, bugs, 'still shows'); 'regression', 'fixed', 'wrong' and 'broken' are not triggers. The check applies only to class code or tests with a capability, no question and a behavior criterion, and matches trimmed non-bullet prose only. The refusal text names the two criteria to add with an example, and `read_for` re-reads once with the refusal as a correction. Corpus and unit Accept cases cover 'a fixed list', 'reports broken links', 'wrong value' and 'add regression tests'. The trigger list lives in one const, so replay can narrow it.

risks.risk: Introspection fix requests all trigger the check, so the share of newly refused readings could exceed the declared 8% and hold the replay at 10%.
risks.mitigation: The scope is stated in the doc comment and CHANGELOG, and corpus case `introspection-fix-request-without-diagnosis` shows it. The 8% is labelled an estimate. If the replay holds, the producer or verifier can narrow the trigger const; the check order and the other rules stay.

risks.risk: A criterion that names a path and says 'root cause' passes without a real diagnosis, or the test uses invented data.
risks.mitigation: The concrete-location and not-a-request-bullet rules remove the copied-boilerplate path. Athena's revert run (run/verification.rs:128) mechanically checks the 'fails without the fix' claim because the gate uses the same predicate. Whether the test uses real approved and rejected data stays prose-only; the guide and doc comment say so.

risks.risk: The location rule accepts a non-location path-like token such as 'and/or'.
risks.mitigation: A `path_tokens` token counts only when its last segment holds a '.', or when it is a crates/ path or a backticked span. A unit test covers 'and/or' alone, which is refused.

risks.risk: Making `asks_for_failing_run_without_the_fix` `pub(crate)` couples the reading gate to a function in the run module; a later change to its wording changes the gate.
risks.mitigation: That coupling is intended. Test F pins the gate's accept set to the predicate, and run/tests.rs:4698 pins the predicate. Both halves move together.

risks.risk: A wrapped bullet's continuation line is read as prose and could carry a repair word.
risks.mitigation: Accepted and noted in the doc comment; the same line shape already limits `request_text_acceptance`.

risks.risk: A new corpus case is refused by an earlier check, so the new check never refuses in the corpus.
risks.mitigation: Cases start from `base_reading`, change class, criterion kinds, assumption and deliverable only, use a `Code survey:` assumption naming a crates/ path present in `repo_files()`, and avoid report/summary wording and job ids. The producer runs the corpus test and reshapes the case, not the check order.

risks.risk: The briefs.rs rule-count test and the `section.len() < 2400` bound fail after a seventh rule and a second guide.
risks.mitigation: Update both in the same change; the producer measures the new section length and sets the bound just above it, with a comment.

risks.risk: This job's own retry is refused by its own gate.
risks.mitigation: Unit test `root_cause_diagnosis_accepts_this_jobs_own_reading` asserts the job's reading shape is accepted.

risks.risk: Queued proposed bug-fix jobs with old stored readings silently leave the drain queue.
risks.mitigation: Documented behavior of `queued_work` (steward.rs:380). The CHANGELOG entry tells the person running Athena that such jobs wait for `athena go`, and the new steward test shows it.

Test A `root_cause_diagnosis_refuses_a_symptom_only_reading`: start from `code_reading(&[SURVEY], &[MODIFY_READING])`, set criteria to one behavior criterion that only describes page content ('Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the page shows only undecided proposals'), with request 'The page lists proposals that were already decided; fix it.'
